body: The `// No hash for virtual methods, go on.` is probably no longer accurate... Or is this what the `@todo` refers to?

Can you imagine that there's any way how the hash is going to change in the future?

Just because I remember the big issue we had with re-hashing methods in 4.0.x, and also a few other cases where it wasn't clear how const-ness and some other properties would affect hashes.
That's what the `@todo` refers to - that `continue` needs to be dropped, and validation added

The hash is computed here the same way as with non-virtual methods.

Hopefully, we won't have to mass change how the hashes are done, but there's always the possibility of fixing bugs in the hashing process, which is why we had those issues previously. If that comes up for virtual methods, I imagine we'll handle it in the same way?

> a few other cases where it wasn't clear how const-ness and some other properties would affect hashes.

Well, `const`-ness does affect the hashes. I think the discussion earlier was about whether it should or not? Since `const`-ness doesn't actually affect binary compatibility, it's a judgement call on our part of whether that should change the hash, but if remember right a number of people (including @vnen?) were in favor of `const`-ness being part of the hash.

Anyway, in this PR it's calculating the hash the same way as with non-virtual methods, which I personally think is fine.
`StringName` has a `hash()` function that I think is guaranteed to be the same as `.operator String().hash()`.
Using a 32-bit hash function for an effective boolean seems a bit suboptimal. `HashMap` uses `hash_fmix32` for `uint8`, but I guess that's probably not a lot better.

The whole of the hashing here is copied from `MethodBind::get_hash()`. It isn't really necessary for virtual methods to be the same as those for non-virtual methods, but I'd prefer them to be, so I'm going to leave this as it is.
Using the same hash method seems fine in the terms of uniformity.
This seems like a sensible decision. Maybe a comment alluding to this would help keep it that way :)

Hm, looking through the code, this _seems_ to be true.

Depending on how a `StringName` is created, it looks like it'll either be hashed via `string.hash()` (which would be exactly the same) or `String::hash(const_char_ptr)` which has code that looks to be the same, but it makes me a little nervous given that the former is using `uint32_t` for the characters and the latter is using `uint8_t`.

In any case, it does seem like they should be the same!

I _think_ we can be sure of this since `StringName` uses the hash to identify itself. But yeah, since this is not at all performance critical, I'll leave it to you if you want to keep it as-is. It's always possible `StringName` wants to swap out its hashing algorithm underneath some time, and I'm not sure if the `StringName` hash is intended to be used outside like this.
I've swapped this for `StringName`'s `hash()` in my latest push. Thanks!
In my latest push, I've added a comment explaining that this functions aims to generate hashes compatible with `MethodBind::get_hash()`. Thanks!

```suggestion
					continue; // Virtual methods didn't use to have hashes, so skip check if it's missing in the old file.
```
Thanks! Updated in latest push
Should we change current usage of `MethodBind::get_hash()` to use `MethodInfo::get_compatibility_hash()` instead, to keep it consistent?
We could. However, the two types of hashes don't necessarily _need_ to be consistent, I'd just prefer them to be, since we've already "battle tested" the hashes from `MethodBind::get_hash()`.

@akien-mga I tried having `MethodBind::get_hash()` use `MethodInfo::get_compatibility_hash()` and it turned up a handful of unrelated bugs :-)

For example, there were some methods that had registered more default arguments than they have arguments, which is incorrect and should be fixed. Fixing this means removing the extra default arguments and adding a compatibility hash.

Here's all the changes:

https://github.com/dsnopek/godot/commit/68d7150a6c0545f77fa36fa9138ad0e1d14aad07

Given that these changes are unrelated to the original goal of this PR, would you prefer (1) that I save those for a follow-up PR or (2) should I merge those changes into this PR anyway?
I think you can save them for a follow-up PR. Looks like a good cleanup!
Ok, thanks!
I just posted PR https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/101449 with these changes
